children: Peter Warren Automotive's property backed balance sheet keeps Morgans neutral on the stock despite near-term demand headwinds for the Australian vehicle dealer. Analyst Jared Gelsomino tells clients in a note that 244 million Australian dollars' worth of property provides downside support amid an increasingly competitive industry structure. He sees Chinese brands continuing to shape the market, adding to pressures from higher gasoline prices and elevated interest rates. Gelsomino says cost savings should help improve its fiscal 2H performance, but worries about industry wide margin pressures. Morgans keeps a hold rating on the stock and cuts its target price 40% to A$0.54. Shares are flat at A$0.545. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
